reason: I'll follow the old stars first to see what happens as the galaxies meet.
expectation: I expect the stars to pass through the other galaxy, though the encounter may change their paths.

alternatives.reason: Bringing the gas clouds together also advances a goal, but I'm more curious about the stars first.

effect: The stars survived the encounter but changed paths, completing their goal; I'll turn to the clouds.
reaction: The distinction between a galaxy losing its shape and its stars avoiding collisions is striking.
reason: Combining the gas clouds is the only available gameplay action and advances the remaining goal.
expectation: I expect the clouds to meet and interact, perhaps compressing gas, though the exact result is uncertain.

effect: The clouds heated and compressed, with some gas gathering further as radiation carried energy away; both goals are complete.
reaction: The contrast with the mostly noncolliding stars was satisfying.

mostWorthwhile.text: Following the old stars was most worthwhile: it showed how gravity can reshape a galaxy without its stars colliding.

leastWorthwhile.text: Combining the clouds was less engaging as a decision because it was the only remaining action, although its explanation was useful.

surprise.text: I was struck that a galaxy can lose its shape while almost all its stars pass between those of the other galaxy.

arbitrary.text: Neither action felt arbitrary; each clearly followed one of the stated goals.

continue.text: Yes, I would continue to see what the gathering gas becomes; the contrasting outcomes for stars and clouds made me curious.
